Q: Project ideas for 14 y/o A:

For web apps, i find very useful to try to implement basic functionalities.

First step:

create basic webapp, expose endpoint, try to debug simple endpoint, see what is HttpContext, how you can use it to interact with incoming HTTP request and HTTP response to return.

Second level

Try adding some middleware, read how the HTTP pipeline works, learn basic concepts of ASP.NET beyond simple endpoints.

Additionally, reading about REST APIs would become useful at this stage.

Third level

Explore further:

  • application configuraiton: env variables, appsetings.json, IOptions pattern
  • explore global error handling

Fourth level

Explore more advanced areas such as authorization and authentication.

Going further

I think above should give you firm idea about ASP.NET.

By that time you should also have better idea what you want to do and what to explore.

I could suggest going deeper to databases, learn SQL and then ORM, such as Entity Framework.

TBC..

Q: Python Selenium download images (jpeg, png) or PDF using ChromeDriver A:

Instead of relying in specific browser / driver options I would implement a more generic solution using the image url to perform the download.

You can get the image URL using similar code:

driver.find_element_by_id("your-image-id").get_attribute("src")

And then I would download the image using, for example, urllib.

Here's some pseudo-code for Python2:

import urllib

url = driver.find_element_by_id("your-image-id").get_attribute("src")
urllib.urlretrieve(url, "local-filename.jpg")

Here's the same for Python3:

import urllib.request

url = driver.find_element_by_id("your-image-id").get_attribute("src")
urllib.request.urlretrieve(url, "local-filename.jpg")

Edit after the comment, just another example about how to download a file once you know its URL:

import requests
from PIL import Image
from io import StringIO

image_name = 'image.jpg'
url = 'http://example.com/image.jpg'

r = requests.get(url)

i = Image.open(StringIO(r.content))
i.save(image_name)

Edit 11/02/2026 A more modern and performant example, using multithreading and multiple file type selector:

from pathlib import Path
import requests
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor, as_completed

from selenium import webdriver
from selenium.webdriver.chrome.options import Options
from selenium.webdriver.common.by import By


def create_driver() -> webdriver.Chrome:
    opts = Options()
    opts.add_argument("--headless=new")
    opts.add_argument("--no-sandbox")
    opts.add_argument("--disable-gpu")
    opts.add_experimental_option(
        "prefs",
        {
            "download.prompt_for_download": False,
            "download.directory_upgrade": True,
            "safebrowsing.enabled": True,
            "plugins.always_open_pdf_externally": True,
        },
    )
    return webdriver.Chrome(options=opts)


def make_session():
    s = requests.Session()
    return s


def download_one(url: str, outdir: Path):
    outdir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    target = outdir / Path(url).name

    with make_session() as s:
        r = s.get(url, stream=True)
        r.raise_for_status()
        with open(target, "wb") as f:
            for chunk in r.iter_content(65536):
                if chunk:
                    f.write(chunk)
    return target


FILE_SELECTOR = (
    "a[href$='.pdf'], "
    "a[href$='.jpg'], a[href$='.jpeg'], a[href$='.png'], a[href$='.gif'], "
    "a[href$='.webp'], a[href$='.svg']"
)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    url = "https://github.com/pdf-association/pdf20examples"
    outdir = Path("downloads")

    driver = create_driver()
    driver.get(url)

    urls = [a.get_attribute("href") for a in driver.find_elements(By.CSS_SELECTOR, FILE_SELECTOR)]
    driver.quit()

    print(f"Found {len(urls)} downloadable files")

    downloaded = []
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=6) as pool:
        futures = [pool.submit(download_one, u, outdir) for u in urls]
        for fut in as_completed(futures):
            downloaded.append(fut.result())

    print("Downloaded:")
    for f in downloaded:
        print(" ->", f.name)

Q: qt QWidget click A:

QWidget does not have a clicked() signal, and QMainWindow does not have an exit() slot. It is impossible to connect to an unexisting signal and unexisting slot. The return value of the connect must be true if the connect is successful. Check this value when you make connections to be sure that your code will work correctly.

To exit your application, you must call qApp->quit()

Also, as it has been mentioned by others, you will have to install an eventFilter or reimplement the 

void QWidget::mousePressEvent ( QMouseEvent * event )   [virtual protected]

or 

void QWidget::mouseReleaseEvent ( QMouseEvent * event )   [virtual protected]

methods.

There are plenty of examples in the official doc of Qt, this for example reimplements the mousePressEvent(QMouseEvent *event) method.

For the eventFilter option, see this small example.

Hope this helps.

Q: jOOQ: how to fetch custom query into a POJO without building one for each query A:

The general purpose type is Record3 (or any other Record[N] type). There aren't any general purpose POJOs in jOOQ 3.20, such as Pojo3. You could use jOOλ or any other third party library that offers general purpose tuple types, assuming this is about not having any dependencies on the jOOQ library from your record types.

Q: How can I encode two numbers in a single Integer? A:

What you are asking is called in mathematics pairing function.

There are many pairing functions, amoung which there are Goedel's, Cantor's, Chinese Remainder Theorem, etc.

Godel p.f. is not practical to encode nested languages, but it's excellent for plain languages with not so many symbols.
